newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Bahia cocoa producers differ over crop estimates.
newsitem.headline: Bahia cocoa producers differ over crop estimates.

text.p: Producer associations in Brazil's key cocoa area of Bahia have conflicting views on the size of the region's upcoming midcrop, with estimates ranging between 800,000 and 1.1 million 60-kg bags.

According to director of the Brazilian Cocoa Producers' Association, the midcrop could drop to as low as 800,000 bags because of dry weather earlier this year and the spread of the lethal witch's broom disease.
"The range is between 800,000 bags and 900,000 bags...But it should be nearer to 800,000 bags," said Jose Mendes.
Good rains since the middle of February have failed to make up for a dry spell during December and January but more worrying is the extent of the damage of witch's broom, Mendes said.

But the president of the National Cocoa Producers' Council (CNPC) believes the recent rains have helped recuperate some previous losses with the result he is now expecting a crop of between 900,000 to 1.1 million bags.
"Without doubt, the outlook is more optimistic," said Wallace Setenta.
Both officials agreed that harvesting of the crop will begin later than usual, with supplies only beginning to trickle in from mid-June. Normally the harvest runs from May to September.
Given previous expectations of a crop of 900,000 bags, producers last month gave their blessing to up to 15,000 of cocoa imports to August, with 6,000 tonnes already booked from Indonesia.
